root_cause: The keyboard navigation uses `adjustDate` which adds/subtracts days without skipping disabled days (weekends when `disableWeekends` is true). This causes the date picker to land on a Saturday (2026-11-21) instead of skipping to Monday (2026-11-23). Additionally, the previous fix incorrectly used a step of 1 day for all arrow keys, breaking week navigation (ArrowUp/ArrowDown).
repair_strategy: Add a helper method `_getNextSelectableDate` to the Pikaday constructor that finds the next selectable date in a given direction (respecting minDate, maxDate, disableWeekends, disableDayFn) by stepping by the given increment (1 for left/right, 7 for up/down). Replace the `adjustDate` calls in the `_onKeyChange` switch with calls to this helper followed by `setDate`.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between selectable dates only; weekends (when disabled) are skipped, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). Arrow keys move by day (left/right) and by week (up/down) while skipping disabled dates.
functional_risks: The helper loops up to 366 steps; if all days are disabled it returns the original date (no change).
The adjustDate public method remains unchanged for programmatic use.
verification_requirements: Run the frozen journey: from Friday 20 Nov, ArrowRight selects Monday 23 Nov.
Regression guard: Arrow keys still move between open days (left, right, up, down).
Verify that minDate/maxDate boundaries are respected.
